scope: Research suitability. KEEP is not a redistribution approval. REPLACE recommends a new research role/source under a new ID; never retarget the existing ID.
limitations: No production DB read or full numerical history reconciliation. Source range metadata and documented breaks were checked; no gap-free or real-time-vintage guarantee.

datasets.name: US CPI price index (SA)
datasets.definition: All-items CPI-U, seasonally adjusted; monthly percent changes are SA; annual SA changes are not the official NSA headline.
datasets.original_identifier: BLS CUSR0000SA0; FRED CPIAUCSL

history.status: verified current FRED metadata range, not gap-free coverage

datasets.revision_methodology: Annual seasonal-factor recalculation can revise the preceding five years. Weights, sampling and methods evolve; preserve release vintages for historical information-set studies.
datasets.suitable_for: Seasonally adjusted short-run consumer-price momentum and inflation-cycle comparisons.
datasets.unsuitable_for: Official NSA annual headline, individual household cost of living, policy announcement timing or point-in-time trading backtests using revised history.
datasets.continuity_and_presentation_risks: Urban-consumer coverage and basket weights evolve; an index level is not an inflation rate. Annual SA changes differ from the official NSA headline.
datasets.alternatives_or_complements: Existing cpi_nsa for official annual CPI; PCEPI for broader consumption prices; BLS release vintages for announcement studies.

datasets.name: US core CPI price index (SA)
datasets.definition: CPI-U excluding food and energy, seasonally adjusted.
datasets.original_identifier: BLS CUSR0000SA0L1E; FRED CPILFESL

history.status: verified current FRED metadata range, not gap-free coverage

datasets.revision_methodology: Annual seasonal-factor recalculation can revise the preceding five years. Weights, sampling and methods evolve; preserve release vintages for historical information-set studies.
datasets.suitable_for: Short-run consumer inflation excluding food and energy.
datasets.unsuitable_for: A complete household inflation burden, pure monetary-policy shock or the NSA core headline without choosing that separate series.
datasets.continuity_and_presentation_risks: Excluding food/energy does not remove every transitory price movement; shelter lags and changing weights matter.
datasets.alternatives_or_complements: Existing core_cpi_nsa and core_pce; Cleveland Fed median/trimmed-mean CPI under their own definitions and terms.

datasets.name: US PCE price index (SA)
datasets.definition: BEA chain-type price index for personal consumption expenditures; annual inflation is the 12-month index change.
datasets.original_source: BEA NIPA / Personal Income and Outlays
datasets.original_identifier: BEA DPCERG; FRED PCEPI

history.status: verified current FRED metadata range, not gap-free coverage

datasets.revision_methodology: Monthly estimates are revised with new inputs and annual/comprehensive NIPA updates. Chain weights, methods and reference years change; current history is not a release-time vintage.
datasets.suitable_for: Broad consumption-price inflation and the price concept relevant to the Fed's longer-run inflation objective.
datasets.unsuitable_for: A substitute for CPI contract escalation, a fixed basket or a release-time policy information set without vintages.
datasets.continuity_and_presentation_risks: Scope, third-party-paid consumption and chain weights differ from CPI; indexes cannot be spliced merely because both measure prices.
datasets.alternatives_or_complements: Existing core_pce for food/energy exclusion and cpi_nsa for a different consumer-price scope; no wholesale replacement needed.

datasets.name: US core PCE price index (SA)
datasets.definition: BEA chain-type PCE prices excluding food and energy.
datasets.original_source: BEA NIPA / Personal Income and Outlays
datasets.original_identifier: BEA DPCCRG; FRED PCEPILFE

history.status: verified current FRED metadata range, not gap-free coverage

datasets.revision_methodology: Monthly estimates are revised with new inputs and annual/comprehensive NIPA updates. Chain weights, methods and reference years change; current history is not a release-time vintage.
datasets.suitable_for: Underlying consumption-price trends excluding food and energy, using the stated transformation.
datasets.unsuitable_for: An exact representation of all inflation faced by households or an unrevised policy-surprise series.
datasets.continuity_and_presentation_risks: Chain weights and comprehensive revisions matter; core PCE and core CPI have different scopes and formulas.
datasets.alternatives_or_complements: Dallas Fed trimmed-mean PCE as a separate robust-trend measure, with source-specific permission review.

datasets.name: US unemployment rate (U-3, SA)
datasets.definition: Civilian unemployed as a percent of the civilian labour force, age 16+, seasonally adjusted.
datasets.original_identifier: BLS LNS14000000; FRED UNRATE

history.status: verified current FRED metadata range, not gap-free coverage

datasets.revision_methodology: Seasonal revisions and population-control updates can change estimates or create breaks; historical treatment differs across levels and rates. Survey redesigns require source notes and vintages.
datasets.suitable_for: U-3 labour-market slack among the civilian labour force aged 16 and over.
datasets.unsuitable_for: The share of the entire population without a job, unique payroll job creation, or all underemployment.
datasets.continuity_and_presentation_risks: Labour-force exits can reduce the rate without employment gains. Annual population controls and redesigns need review.
datasets.alternatives_or_complements: U-6 (U6RATE), prime-age employment/population (LNS12300060), and existing participation/payrolls; each is a distinct concept.

datasets.name: US total nonfarm payroll employment (level, SA)
datasets.definition: CES establishment-survey total nonfarm employment level in thousands of persons; monthly jobs change is adjacent-month difference times 1,000.
datasets.original_identifier: BLS CES0000000001; FRED PAYEMS

history.status: verified current FRED metadata range, not gap-free coverage

datasets.revision_methodology: Initial estimates normally receive two monthly revisions; annual employment benchmarking, seasonal factors and methodological updates revise history. Changes in job mix matter for average earnings.
datasets.suitable_for: Establishment nonfarm payroll job levels and correctly scaled adjacent-month job changes.
datasets.unsuitable_for: Unique employed people, self-employment, a fixed unrevised jobs-announcement surprise or direct wage purchasing power.
datasets.continuity_and_presentation_risks: Multiple jobholders may be counted more than once; employment benchmarks and business births/deaths affect revisions.
datasets.alternatives_or_complements: CPS employment for people, QCEW for benchmarking, and original BLS release archives for announcement-time values.

datasets.name: US real GDP growth (q/q annualized)
datasets.definition: BEA real GDP percent change from preceding quarter, seasonally adjusted at annual rates. Already a growth rate, not a GDP level or YoY change.
datasets.original_identifier: BEA A191RL; FRED A191RL1Q225SBEA

history.status: verified current FRED metadata range, not gap-free coverage

datasets.revision_methodology: Advance, second and third quarterly estimates, followed by annual/comprehensive revisions. Annualized growth is already transformed; inspect vintage and reference-year changes.
datasets.suitable_for: Quarter-on-quarter annualized real US output growth.
datasets.unsuitable_for: A GDP level, ordinary quarterly percent change, year-on-year growth or a monthly activity observation.
datasets.continuity_and_presentation_risks: Already annualized: do not apply another percentage-change transform or sum rates as though they were dollars.
datasets.alternatives_or_complements: GDPC1 real GDP level for consistent YoY/level questions; final sales and GDI for complementary output evidence.

datasets.name: Monthly average effective federal funds rate
datasets.definition: Monthly average of daily effective federal funds rates, percent, NSA. Not the daily effective rate and not the FOMC target range.
datasets.original_source: Federal Reserve Board; underlying daily effective rates administered by New York Fed
datasets.original_identifier: Board H.15 effective funds monthly; FRED FEDFUNDS

history.status: verified current FRED metadata range, not gap-free coverage

datasets.revision_methodology: Official monthly aggregation of daily effective rates. Daily methodology changed from brokered volume-weighted mean to FR 2420 transaction-based volume-weighted median on 2016-03-01; monthly figures include calendar days.
datasets.suitable_for: Monthly overnight funding conditions and slow-moving policy-regime context.
datasets.unsuitable_for: Identifying first hike/cut announcement dates, target rates, daily event returns or monetary-policy surprises.
datasets.continuity_and_presentation_risks: Averages mix before/after a decision and calendar-day weights. The 2016 calculation break is distinct from target-regime changes.
datasets.alternatives_or_complements: Official FOMC statements/events; DFEDTAR and DFEDTARL/U for target states; DFF or NY Fed EFFR for daily implementation.

datasets.name: S&P 500 price index
datasets.definition: S&P 500 price index closing value; excludes dividends and is not itself a tradeable security.
datasets.original_source: S&P Dow Jones Indices; Yahoo redistributor
datasets.original_identifier: S&P DJI S&P 500 price index; secondary Yahoo ^GSPC

history.status: secondary vendor firstTradeDate only; contract/backcast continuity and actual endpoint span unverified

datasets.revision_methodology: Secondary-vendor corrections and backcasts are not a versioned original index archive. Price indexes exclude dividends; historical constituent/basket changes require original methodology.
datasets.suitable_for: Qualified US large-cap price-index context after feed validation and permission clearance.
datasets.unsuitable_for: Dividend-inclusive investor performance, a tradable security or an unqualified pre-launch/live-constituent history.
datasets.continuity_and_presentation_risks: Modern 500-stock index launched in 1957; earlier vendor history is a predecessor/backcast question. Yahoo firstTradeDate does not prove uniform construction.
datasets.alternatives_or_complements: Licensed original S&P price and total-return series; a separately identified SPY total-return proxy only with dividends, fees, tracking and its 1993 inception disclosed.

datasets.name: Gold — continuous futures
datasets.definition: Yahoo GC=F continuous/front-contract history, USD per troy ounce. Neither spot gold nor a verified exchange settlement.
datasets.original_source: COMEX/CME contract market; vendor continuation construction not verified
datasets.original_identifier: COMEX GC underlying contract; vendor Yahoo GC=F continuation

history.status: secondary vendor firstTradeDate only; contract/backcast continuity and actual endpoint span unverified

datasets.revision_methodology: Per-bar contract selection, roll date, adjustment method and close/settlement identity are not established by the current adapter. Current history is not a frozen contract-level audit trail.
datasets.suitable_for: Clearly qualified futures-price exploration, pending contract-map, close-time and rights validation.
datasets.unsuitable_for: Primary spot-gold benchmark, documented rolled futures strategy returns or announcement-window inference from the date label alone.
datasets.continuity_and_presentation_risks: Basis/carry and contract switches can contaminate chained-close returns. Vendor metadata starts 2000-08-30; it cannot cover 1994/1999 cycle windows. COMEX settlement is not a post-14:00 ET quote.
datasets.alternatives_or_complements: New licensed London gold AM/PM benchmark IDs for spot research; licensed timestamped XAU/USD or explicit single-contract futures for narrow FOMC windows. Retain gold unchanged as the legacy futures ID.

datasets.name: US 10Y Treasury constant-maturity yield
datasets.definition: H.15 nominal 10-year constant-maturity Treasury yield quoted in percent per annum, not a bond price or total return.
datasets.original_source: Federal Reserve Board / US Treasury yield-curve inputs
datasets.original_identifier: Board H.15 / Treasury 10-year constant maturity; FRED DGS10

history.status: verified current FRED metadata range, not gap-free coverage

datasets.revision_methodology: Correction-prone financial observations rather than macro survey vintages. Missing business-day quotes must remain missing; yields are fitted constant-maturity estimates, not tradable bond returns.
datasets.suitable_for: Nominal long-term yield conditions and basis-point changes.
datasets.unsuitable_for: A real yield, a bond price/total return or a timestamp-synchronous intraday control.
datasets.continuity_and_presentation_risks: Constant maturity is fitted, not a held bond. Curve/input methods and holiday gaps matter.
datasets.alternatives_or_complements: DFII10 real TIPS yield, DGS2 short-end expectations, and separate 10-year breakevens for decomposition.

datasets.name: ICE US Dollar Index (price index)
datasets.definition: Yahoo DX-Y.NYB index history. Not the dollar-index futures contract, an FX pair or a tradeable total-return product.
datasets.original_identifier: ICE USDX cash index; secondary Yahoo DX-Y.NYB

history.status: secondary vendor firstTradeDate only; contract/backcast continuity and actual endpoint span unverified

datasets.revision_methodology: Secondary-vendor corrections and backcasts are not a versioned original index archive. Price indexes exclude dividends; historical constituent/basket changes require original methodology.
datasets.suitable_for: A fixed developed-currency-basket dollar measure with clear ICE attribution and cleared rights.
datasets.unsuitable_for: The broad trade-weighted dollar, an FX pair, index futures returns or all US trading-partner exposure.
datasets.continuity_and_presentation_risks: Six-currency basket, euro weight 57.6%; 1999 euro transition. Vendor firstTradeDate precedes the 1973 base/launch convention, so backcasts require proof.
datasets.alternatives_or_complements: DTWEXBGS nominal broad trade-weighted dollar (2006 onward); separate historical DTWEXM/DTWEXB panels, never a silent splice.

datasets.name: WTI crude oil — continuous futures
datasets.definition: Yahoo CL=F continuous/front-contract history, USD per barrel. Neither spot WTI nor a verified exchange settlement. Signed historical prices are valid.
datasets.original_source: NYMEX/CME contract market; vendor continuation construction not verified
datasets.original_identifier: NYMEX CL underlying contract; vendor Yahoo CL=F continuation

history.status: secondary vendor firstTradeDate only; contract/backcast continuity and actual endpoint span unverified

datasets.revision_methodology: Per-bar contract selection, roll date, adjustment method and close/settlement identity are not established by the current adapter. Current history is not a frozen contract-level audit trail.
datasets.suitable_for: Qualified signed futures-price context, with explicit roll and delivery caveats.
datasets.unsuitable_for: Default physical spot-oil benchmark, physical production/consumption quantities or chained strategy returns without a roll specification.
datasets.continuity_and_presentation_risks: Vendor metadata starts 2000-08-23; April 2020 expiry/storage effects and legitimate negative prices defeat generic log/percentage-return assumptions.
datasets.alternatives_or_complements: EIA Cushing WTI spot, FRED comparison identifier DCOILWTICO, under a new ID; add inventories/production/consumption separately. Preserve wti as futures.

datasets.name: US CPI price index (NSA)
datasets.definition: BLS all-items CPI-U, not seasonally adjusted; official annual headline uses comparable month one year earlier.
datasets.original_identifier: BLS CUUR0000SA0; FRED CPIAUCNS

history.status: verified current FRED metadata range, not gap-free coverage

datasets.revision_methodology: No routine seasonal-factor revision; corrections and methodological/coverage changes remain possible. Do not describe the series as immutable.
datasets.suitable_for: Official all-items 12-month CPI inflation, purchasing-power comparisons with caveats, and the specified NSA escalation concept.
datasets.unsuitable_for: Seasonally adjusted monthly momentum or an individual household's exact inflation experience.
datasets.continuity_and_presentation_risks: Seasonality affects short-horizon changes; annual weight/method changes do not make the index a fixed historical basket.
datasets.alternatives_or_complements: Existing cpi for SA month-on-month analysis and pce for a broader consumption-price concept; no replacement needed.

datasets.name: US core CPI price index (NSA)
datasets.definition: BLS CPI-U excluding food and energy, NSA; official annual core inflation uses comparable month one year earlier.
datasets.original_identifier: BLS CUUR0000SA0L1E; FRED CPILFENS

history.status: verified current FRED metadata range, not gap-free coverage

datasets.revision_methodology: No routine seasonal-factor revision; corrections and methodological/coverage changes remain possible. Do not describe the series as immutable.
datasets.suitable_for: Official 12-month CPI excluding food and energy.
datasets.unsuitable_for: All household price pressure, SA monthly core momentum or a real-time surprise without the actual release vintage.
datasets.continuity_and_presentation_risks: Core composition/weights change; short NSA month-to-month moves retain seasonality.
datasets.alternatives_or_complements: Existing core_cpi for SA monthly momentum and core_pce for a different scope; no silent blending.

datasets.name: Initial unemployment claims
datasets.definition: New unemployment-insurance claims, seasonally adjusted, week ending Saturday; not continuing claims.
datasets.original_source: US Department of Labor Employment and Training Administration
datasets.original_identifier: DOL ETA UI Weekly Claims / initial SA; FRED ICSA

history.status: verified current FRED metadata range, not gap-free coverage

datasets.revision_methodology: Recent weeks can be revised; seasonal factors and estimation methods are updated. Pandemic distortions and reporting backlogs make a single weekly change noisy.
datasets.suitable_for: Timely weekly signals of insured layoffs and labour-market deterioration.
datasets.unsuitable_for: The total unemployed population, all layoffs, or a complete monthly labour-market count.
datasets.continuity_and_presentation_risks: Week ending Saturday is a reference period, not Thursday publication. Seasonality, holidays, backlog and state reporting can distort individual weeks.
datasets.alternatives_or_complements: Initial NSA claims (ICNSA), continuing claims (CCSA) and a clearly labelled four-week average, not fabricated daily interpolation.

datasets.name: Job openings, total nonfarm
datasets.definition: JOLTS total nonfarm job openings, level in thousands, seasonally adjusted; distinct from payroll job creation.
datasets.original_source: BLS Job Openings and Labor Turnover Survey
datasets.original_identifier: BLS JOLTS total nonfarm openings; FRED JTSJOL

history.status: verified current FRED metadata range, not gap-free coverage

datasets.revision_methodology: Preliminary estimates receive revisions and annual benchmarking/seasonal updates. Scope is surveyed vacancies, not all internet advertisements.
datasets.suitable_for: Surveyed unfilled positions at the last business day of the month and vacancy demand.
datasets.unsuitable_for: Payroll jobs created, monthly hires, exact online vacancy advertisements or a real-time count of all available jobs.
datasets.continuity_and_presentation_risks: Stock at a reference date, not an average flow. Vacancy levels and rates answer different questions as the employment base changes.
datasets.alternatives_or_complements: JTSJOR vacancy rate, JTSHIR hires and JTSQUR quits rate; preserve stock/flow definitions separately.

datasets.name: Labour-force participation rate
datasets.definition: Civilian labour force as a share of civilian noninstitutional population aged 16+, seasonally adjusted.
datasets.original_identifier: BLS LNS11300000; FRED CIVPART

history.status: verified current FRED metadata range, not gap-free coverage

datasets.revision_methodology: Seasonal revisions and population-control updates can change estimates or create breaks; historical treatment differs across levels and rates. Survey redesigns require source notes and vintages.
datasets.suitable_for: Civilian labour-force participation among the noninstitutional population aged 16+.
datasets.unsuitable_for: Unemployment, employment/population or a pure cyclical slack measure unaffected by ageing.
datasets.continuity_and_presentation_risks: Demographic composition and population controls matter; denominator scope differs from payroll employment.
datasets.alternatives_or_complements: Prime-age participation (LNS11300060), prime-age employment/population and existing unemployment.

datasets.name: Average hourly earnings, total private
datasets.definition: Average nominal hourly earnings of all private employees; excludes benefits and is not inflation-adjusted or a fixed-composition wage index.
datasets.original_identifier: BLS CES0500000003; same FRED identifier

history.status: verified current FRED metadata range, not gap-free coverage

datasets.revision_methodology: Initial estimates normally receive two monthly revisions; annual employment benchmarking, seasonal factors and methodological updates revise history. Changes in job mix matter for average earnings.
datasets.suitable_for: Average nominal gross hourly earnings of all private payroll employees.
datasets.unsuitable_for: Fixed-composition wage inflation, benefits-inclusive compensation, median earnings or real purchasing power without an explicit deflator.
datasets.continuity_and_presentation_risks: Job-composition shocks can raise the average while low-paid workers lose jobs. All-employee scope differs from longer production/nonsupervisory series.
datasets.alternatives_or_complements: Employment Cost Index wage/compensation measures; separately deflated real earnings and the older nonsupervisory series with its narrower scope.

datasets.name: 5-year breakeven inflation rate
datasets.definition: Nominal-minus-inflation-indexed 5-year Treasury yield spread. Includes inflation risk and liquidity premia; not pure expected inflation.
datasets.original_source: Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis calculation, Treasury yield inputs
datasets.original_identifier: St. Louis Fed DGS5 minus DFII5; FRED T5YIE

history.status: verified current FRED metadata range, not gap-free coverage

datasets.revision_methodology: Derived from Treasury yield inputs; corrections and input-method/source changes propagate. FRED notes a Treasury input-source change in June 2019 for breakevens. Negative spreads/real yields are legitimate.
datasets.suitable_for: Market-based five-year inflation compensation and comparison with nominal/real yields.
datasets.unsuitable_for: A pure survey expectation, realized future inflation, or the real-yield variable itself.
datasets.continuity_and_presentation_risks: Inflation risk and TIPS liquidity premia matter, especially under stress. Maturity and quote times must match; no pre-2003 backfill from future CPI.
datasets.alternatives_or_complements: DFII5, DGS5 and a separately permissioned SPF inflation forecast at its own horizon/frequency.

datasets.name: Retail and food-services sales
datasets.definition: Advance nominal retail and food-services sales, seasonally adjusted, not price-adjusted consumption.
datasets.original_identifier: Census Advance Monthly Retail Trade / total retail and food services; FRED RSAFS

history.status: verified current FRED metadata range, not gap-free coverage

datasets.revision_methodology: Advance estimates are revised as fuller monthly information and annual benchmark inputs arrive; historical corrections and seasonal/trading-day factors can change the full path.
datasets.suitable_for: Nominal retail/food-service spending and near-term goods-oriented demand.
datasets.unsuitable_for: Real sales volume, all household services consumption, material tonnage or a standalone real-consumption measure.
datasets.continuity_and_presentation_risks: Seasonal/trading-day adjustment is not inflation adjustment. Industry definitions and annual benchmarks can revise history.
datasets.alternatives_or_complements: Real PCE and explicit goods/services components; a correctly matched retail deflator only under a new documented derived series.

datasets.name: Real personal consumption expenditures
datasets.definition: Real personal consumption expenditures, chained 2017 dollars at seasonally adjusted annual rate; monthly growth is not annualized.
datasets.original_source: BEA NIPA / Personal Income and Outlays
datasets.original_identifier: BEA DPCERX; FRED PCEC96

history.status: verified current FRED metadata range, not gap-free coverage

datasets.revision_methodology: Monthly estimates and annual/comprehensive revisions; chain-linking and rebasing affect reported levels. Chained-dollar components are generally not additive outside the reference period.
datasets.suitable_for: Broad inflation-adjusted household-consumption activity, including services.
datasets.unsuitable_for: Nominal retail sales, physical tonnes of consumption, or an additive sum of all chained-dollar components.
datasets.continuity_and_presentation_risks: Verified current FRED table begins in 2007; do not advertise 1959 coverage without a separately validated source response. SAAR levels do not make monthly growth annualized.
datasets.alternatives_or_complements: BEA direct account/history and real goods/services components; validate the exact monthly table/endpoint mapping before extending history.

datasets.name: University of Michigan consumer sentiment
datasets.definition: University of Michigan survey sentiment index; FRED availability may lag the survey release and licensing applies.
datasets.original_source: University of Michigan Surveys of Consumers
datasets.original_identifier: University of Michigan Index of Consumer Sentiment; FRED UMCSENT

history.status: verified current FRED metadata range, not gap-free coverage

datasets.revision_methodology: Preliminary/final survey readings differ; FRED delivery is delayed one month. Early pre-1978 history is sparse. Telephone-to-web transition April-July 2024 introduces method effects.
datasets.suitable_for: Qualified household attitudes and sentiment, using source-release and delivery-lag information.
datasets.unsuitable_for: Actual spending/output, a live same-month FRED reading, or a homogeneous monthly sample back to the first 1952 observation.
datasets.continuity_and_presentation_risks: Do not fill sparse early observations or interpret the April-July 2024 survey-mode change as wholly economic. Follow the specified source attribution.
datasets.alternatives_or_complements: Separate expectations/current-conditions components if rights-cleared; NY Fed consumer expectations as a different concept, not a drop-in replacement.

datasets.name: Housing starts, total units
datasets.definition: New privately-owned housing units started, thousands at SAAR; not the count physically started during that month.
datasets.original_identifier: Census/HUD New Residential Construction, total privately owned starts; FRED HOUST

history.status: verified current FRED metadata range, not gap-free coverage

datasets.revision_methodology: Survey/administrative estimates receive monthly and annual seasonal revisions. Geographic coverage, authorizations, starts and completions are different populations/stages.
datasets.suitable_for: Residential construction starts and forward demand for housing-related inputs.
datasets.unsuitable_for: All construction/infrastructure activity, completed dwellings, material consumption tonnage or the raw number started during the month.
datasets.continuity_and_presentation_risks: Thousands at SAAR; weather, sampling error and multifamily volatility matter. Use an NSA series for literal monthly counts.
datasets.alternatives_or_complements: Existing permits, single/multifamily components, completions (COMPUTSA) and construction put-in-place spending.

datasets.name: Building permits, total units
datasets.definition: New privately-owned housing units authorized in permit-issuing places, thousands at SAAR; not completed construction.
datasets.original_identifier: Census/HUD Building Permits Survey, total privately owned authorizations; FRED PERMIT

history.status: verified current FRED metadata range, not gap-free coverage

datasets.revision_methodology: Survey/administrative estimates receive monthly and annual seasonal revisions. Geographic coverage, authorizations, starts and completions are different populations/stages.
datasets.suitable_for: Authorized residential pipeline in permit-issuing places.
datasets.unsuitable_for: Starts/completions, all US building work, nonresidential infrastructure or tonnes of aggregate demand.
datasets.continuity_and_presentation_risks: SAAR units and permit-issuing geography must be retained. An authorization does not guarantee subsequent construction.
datasets.alternatives_or_complements: Existing starts; completions, nonresidential/public construction spending and Missouri/local BPS under separate regional selectors.

datasets.name: 30-year fixed mortgage rate
datasets.definition: Freddie Mac PMMS 30-year fixed mortgage average; weekly provider labels, usually Thursday with historical Friday labels. Methodology changed in November 2022; not an individual borrower quote.
datasets.original_identifier: Freddie Mac PMMS 30-year fixed-rate national average; FRED MORTGAGE30US

history.status: verified current FRED metadata range, not gap-free coverage

datasets.revision_methodology: Weekly estimates and corrections; major shift from the prior survey to application-based data on 2022-11-17. Historical publication weekdays differ; do not force Thursday labels backward.
datasets.suitable_for: Broad weekly mortgage financing conditions for the defined borrower/product sample.
datasets.unsuitable_for: Every borrower's available rate, daily policy-event response, APR or a homogeneous unchanged survey methodology across November 2022.
datasets.continuity_and_presentation_risks: Rates/points/sample selection and the 2022 method break matter. Follow actual release/reference weekdays rather than manufacturing a weekly grid.
datasets.alternatives_or_complements: 15-year PMMS and rate/points distributions where permitted; mortgage credit availability and lending standards as different explanatory variables.

datasets.name: Industrial production, total index
datasets.definition: Federal Reserve total industrial production index, 2017=100, seasonally adjusted; distinct from price indexes using the same base year.
datasets.original_identifier: Board G.17 total industrial production; FRED INDPRO

history.status: verified current FRED metadata range, not gap-free coverage

datasets.revision_methodology: Recent monthly estimates, annual benchmarks, seasonal factors, industry weights and methods are revised. Rebased index levels are not tonnes or construction output.
datasets.suitable_for: Real manufacturing/mining/utilities output-cycle context.
datasets.unsuitable_for: Economy-wide GDP, construction output or physical tonnes of one commodity.
datasets.continuity_and_presentation_risks: Industry weights, energy/weather effects and annual benchmarks matter; an index with a 2017 base is not the same economic object as a price index.
datasets.alternatives_or_complements: Manufacturing/mining/utilities components, capacity utilization (TCU) and genuinely physical commodity production/stock datasets.

datasets.name: 10-year minus 2-year Treasury spread
datasets.definition: 10-year minus 2-year nominal constant-maturity Treasury yields, quoted in percentage points; can be negative. Not a recession forecast.
datasets.original_source: Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis calculation, Treasury yield inputs
datasets.original_identifier: St. Louis Fed DGS10 minus DGS2; FRED T10Y2Y

history.status: verified current FRED metadata range, not gap-free coverage

datasets.revision_methodology: Derived from Treasury yield inputs; corrections and input-method/source changes propagate. FRED notes a Treasury input-source change in June 2019 for breakevens. Negative spreads/real yields are legitimate.
datasets.suitable_for: Nominal Treasury curve slope and inversion regimes.
datasets.unsuitable_for: A causal recession forecast, term premium alone, a bond return or a pure expected policy path.

datasets.name: US high-yield credit spread
datasets.definition: ICE BofA US high-yield option-adjusted spread over a spot Treasury curve, percent. Not default probability; FRED currently provides about three years of history and ICE licensing applies.
datasets.original_identifier: ICE BofA US High Yield Index OAS; FRED BAMLH0A0HYM2

history.status: verified current FRED metadata range, not gap-free coverage

datasets.revision_methodology: Constituents rebalance and pricing/OAS models can change; historical corrections are possible. Current FRED access is a rolling three-year window from April 2026, not the index's full economic history.
datasets.suitable_for: Licensed recent speculative-grade credit-risk/financial-conditions context.
datasets.unsuitable_for: Default probability, corporate financing cost for every issuer, a bond total return or a free full-history 2008-cycle study.
datasets.continuity_and_presentation_risks: Current three-year FRED window, model/constituent changes and stale/illiquid bond marks limit interpretation. Levels are quoted percent spreads; changes should be bp/pp.
datasets.alternatives_or_complements: Licensed original ICE history; a distinct reviewed corporate-minus-Treasury spread or published financial-conditions index, never falsely called the same OAS.

datasets.name: US investment-grade corporate spread
datasets.definition: ICE BofA US corporate index option-adjusted spread, percent; investment-grade corporate universe. Not a credit default probability; limited FRED history and ICE licensing apply.
datasets.original_identifier: ICE BofA US Corporate Index OAS; FRED BAMLC0A0CM

datasets.revision_methodology: Constituents rebalance and pricing/OAS models can change; historical corrections are possible. Current FRED access is a rolling three-year window from April 2026, not the index's full economic history.
datasets.suitable_for: Licensed recent investment-grade credit conditions, distinguished from high yield.
datasets.unsuitable_for: A default probability, total return, exact funding rate or unrestricted long-history cycle comparator.
datasets.continuity_and_presentation_risks: Rolling three-year FRED access and changing index constituents/models; Treasury-curve-relative option adjustment is not the same as a simple yield spread.
datasets.alternatives_or_complements: Licensed original ICE history; distinct matched-maturity corporate/Treasury measures with their own IDs and permissions.
